change.title: npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too

source.quote: * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

tasks.reasoning:
The repo pins @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.122.0 in package-lock.json, inside the affected range (<1.0.0). Nothing breaks today, because old SDKs keep sending 2023-06-01, but the 1.0.0 major is the path to the new API version. Neither Anthropic call site sends temperature, top_p or top_k; the temperature in mcp/insights.js goes to the OpenRouter request. The code is JavaScript, so the MessageParam union change is a typing change only. During the upgrade, the migration agent should check two things. First, that the request bodies built in api/ai.js do not pass sampling params or document/citation blocks through from the client. Second, that the thinking and output_config shapes still validate under 2026-10-21. Any Bedrock or Vertex SDK packages would also need v1, but none are recorded in this repo.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- anthropic:2026-10-21-api-version-2026-10-21 (api-version): New Claude API version 2026-10-21 (anthropic-version header); SDKs older than the new majors keep sending 2023-06-01. The repo's SDK (0.122.0) keeps sending anthropic-version 2023-06-01. The move to 2026-10-21 happens through the SDK 1.0.0 upgrade, which sends the new version by default, so the version bump and the SDK bump are one edit.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "This guide lists the code changes for moving from API version `2023-06-01` to `2026-10-21`."
- anthropic:2026-10-14-ts-sdk-otel-default (other): TypeScript SDK 0.134.0 auto-creates OpenTelemetry spans and trace headers if a global tracer provider exists (unsure if affects; opt out with openTelemetry:false). This only applies once the SDK moves past 0.134.0, which the 1.0.0 upgrade does. While upgrading, check whether a global OpenTelemetry tracer provider is registered. If one is and the spans are unwanted, pass openTelemetry:false to the client.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "If your app registers a global tracer provider, the SDK will create spans with it after upgrading, and they'll be exported with the rest of your traces."

callSites.why: Calls messages.create through @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.122.0. After 1.0.0 it runs on API version 2026-10-21, and the MessageParam typing changes for the messages it builds.
Calls messages.create through @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.122.0, which the 1.0.0 upgrade will move to API version 2026-10-21.

## npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too [Verified]

### Change

Bumped @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.122.0 -> ^1.0.0 via npm (installed 1.0.0). No code changes needed: both call sites (api/ai.js, mcp/insights.js) send no temperature/top_p/top_k, no document/citation blocks, and already read content by filtering text blocks. Added test/sdk.test.js, which drives both real call sites with a stubbed fetch and asserts anthropic-version 2026-10-21 and no sampling params in the body (the client's temperature in the request is not forwarded). OTel: no tracer provider registered, so left default. No Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry packages, no raw HTTP to api.anthropic.com. The `temperature` in mcp/insights.js goes to OpenRouter only. License of the SDK changes MIT -> Apache-2.0.

Files touched:
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `test/sdk.test.js`

### Why

SDK 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default, which rejects sampling params; the repo needed the bump and confirmation that its requests are compliant.

> * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sdk-proof | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- sdk-proof, added by the agent: `node test/sdk.test.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `sdk-proof`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Real API behaviour at 2026-10-21 for thinking:{type:'adaptive'} and output_config:{effort:'low'}
- Pinned model id claude-opus-5 validity
- Baseline failure of the proof test is just a missing-file/old-SDK failure
- npm audit reports 9 unrelated vulnerabilities, not addressed
- Package-lock churn beyond the SDK was not individually reviewed
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Requests now carry anthropic-version 2026-10-21 instead of 2023-06-01
- SDK license MIT -> Apache-2.0

review.summary: The only change is the @anthropic-ai/sdk bump from ^0.122.0 to ^1.0.0. Neither call site is edited. That is plausible, because api/ai.js:43 and mcp/insights.js:24 already omit temperature/top_p/top_k, pass plain {role, content} messages, and filter response blocks by type === 'text'. The new test does confirm both call sites send anthropic-version 2026-10-21 and no sampling params. But it replaces the SDK's CommonJS export with a wrapper that tries `mod.default || mod`, so it never proves that the app's own `const Anthropic = require('@anthropic-ai/sdk'); new Anthropic()` still works against 1.0.0. Every request also goes to a stubbed fetch, so nothing shows the live 2026-10-21 API accepts `thinking: {type:'adaptive'}` and `output_config: {effort:'low'}`. Given that, 'verified' rests on a weaker check than it looks.

concerns.issue: The Module._load hook returns a wrapper built from `mod.default || mod` whenever the app requires '@anthropic-ai/sdk'. This hides a real risk in a major bump: api/ai.js:27 and mcp/insights.js:23 call `new Anthropic()` directly on the result of `require()`. If 1.0.0's CJS entry exports a namespace object rather than a constructible class, production breaks with 'Anthropic is not a constructor', yet this test still passes.

`thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }`, `output_config: { effort: 'low' }` and model 'claude-opus-5' are sent unchanged under the new default API version 2026-10-21. The test's fetch stub accepts any body, so server acceptance is unproven. I could not confirm these parameters are valid under 2026-10-21; check the 1.0.0 SDK's MessageCreateParams types and the API version notes. The same applies to mcp/insights.js:24.

Response handling only checks stop_reason === 'refusal' and keeps text blocks. If 2026-10-21 changes stop_reason values or the response content shape, the stubbed response in the test (shaped like the old API) would not catch it.
The new test is not wired into a script; `test` still echoes an error and exits 1. The check only runs if CI calls test/sdk.test.js explicitly.

The SDK's license changes from MIT to Apache-2.0, and it pulls in a new transitive dependency, @opentelemetry/api@1.10.0. This is not forced by the code changes; flag it for license and dependency review.

checkFirst: Run `node -e "const A=require('@anthropic-ai/sdk'); new A({apiKey:'x'})"` with 1.0.0 installed to confirm the plain CJS require is still constructible, without the test's `.default` fallback.
Check the 1.0.0 SDK's MessageCreateParams types or the 2026-10-21 changelog for `thinking.type: 'adaptive'` and `output_config.effort`.
Make one live call per call site (api/ai.js handler, generateInsights) against the real API with 1.0.0 before trusting the 'verified' grade.
Confirm the Apache-2.0 license and the new @opentelemetry/api dependency are acceptable for this MIT project.
